101.subtopic: Negation, Equivalence, Tautology, and Switch Circuits
101.solution:
Since \(p \vee \sim p \equiv T\), option D gives \((\sim q \land p) \vee (p \vee \sim p) \equiv (\sim q \land p) \vee T \equiv T\).
Hence it is a tautology.

102.subtopic: Continuity at a Point — Finding Parameters
102.solution:
\(f(x) = \frac{(x-1)(x+1)(x-2)(x+2)}{|x-1||x-2|}\) for \(x \neq 1,2\).
Since \(\lim_{x\to 1}\frac{x-1}{|x-1|}\) and \(\lim_{x\to 2}\frac{x-2}{|x-2|}\) do not exist, \(f\) is discontinuous at \(x=1,2\).
Elsewhere it is a ratio of polynomials, hence continuous on \(\mathbb{R} - \{1,2\}\).

103.subtopic: Rate of Change and Related Rates
103.solution:
Areas: \(A_1 = x^2,\ A_2 = y^2\).
\(\frac{dA_2}{dA_1} = \frac{2y\,dy/dt}{2x\,dx/dt} = \frac{y}{x}\cdot\frac{dy}{dx}\).
With \(y = x - x^2,\ \frac{dy}{dx} = 1-2x\), so \(\frac{dA_2}{dA_1} = (1-x)(1-2x) = 2x^2 - 3x + 1\).

104.subtopic: Equation of Line — Rotation, Angle, and Bisector
104.solution:
Line with equal intercepts \(x+y=a\) has slope \(m_1 = -1\); the line \(4x-2y+13=0\) has slope \(m_2 = 2\).
\(\tan\theta = \left|\frac{-1-2}{1+(-1)(2)}\right| = 3\), so \(\theta = \tan^{-1}(3)\).

105.subtopic: Symmetry, King's Property, and Absolute Value
105.solution:
Split at \(x=\tfrac12\): \(\int_0^1 x\left|x-\tfrac12\right|dx = \int_0^{1/2}\left(\tfrac12 x - x^2\right)dx + \int_{1/2}^1\left(x^2 - \tfrac12 x\right)dx\).
Evaluating gives \(\frac{1}{8}\).

Let \(p = ax + \frac{bc^2}{x}\) using \(xy=c^2\).
\(\frac{dp}{dx} = a - \frac{bc^2}{x^2} = 0 \Rightarrow x = c\sqrt{\frac{b}{a}}\) (minimum).
Minimum value \(= c\sqrt{ab} + c\sqrt{ab} = 2c\sqrt{ab}\).

109.solution:
Write as \(\frac{\frac{e^{x^2}-1}{x^2} + \frac{1-\cos 3x}{x^2}}{\frac{\sin x}{x}\cdot\frac{\log(1+2x)}{2x}\cdot 2}\).
Using \(\frac{e^{x^2}-1}{x^2}\to 1,\ \frac{1-\cos 3x}{x^2}\to\frac{9}{2}\), the limit \(= \frac{1 + 9/2}{1\cdot 1\cdot 2} = \frac{11}{4}\).

110.solution:
Using \(\int_0^{\pi/2}\frac{a\sin x + b\cos x}{\sin x + \cos x}dx = \frac{\pi}{4}(a+b)\):
\(\int_0^{\pi/2}\frac{300\sin x + 100\cos x}{\sin x + \cos x}dx = \frac{\pi}{4}(300+100) = 100\pi\).

Solution \(y = -x + 4 + ce^x\); through \((0,2)\Rightarrow c=-2\), so \(y = 4 - x - 2e^x\).

119.solution:
Let \(z = x + iy\). \(|z| + z = 3 + i \Rightarrow y = 1\) and \(|z| + x = 3\).
With \(|z| = \sqrt{x^2+1}\): \((3-x)^2 = x^2 + 1 \Rightarrow x = \frac43\), so \(|z| = 3 - \frac43 = \frac53\).

120.solution:

Solution: \(y(1+x)e^{-x} = xe^{-x} + c \Rightarrow y(1+x) = x + ce^x\).

121.solution:
\(\frac{1}{\sin^2 x\cos^2 x} = \frac{\sin^2 x + \cos^2 x}{\sin^2 x\cos^2 x} = \sec^2 x + \csc^2 x\).
\(\int(\sec^2 x + \csc^2 x)dx = \tan x - \cot x + c\).

For B: \(\frac{P_B}{20000} = \left(\frac75\right)^2 = \frac{49}{25}\Rightarrow P_B = 39200\).

129.solution:
Equal projections on \(\bar a\) give \((\bar b - \bar c)\cdot\bar a = 0\).
\(|\bar a + \bar b - \bar c|^2 = |\bar a|^2 + |\bar b|^2 + |\bar c|^2 - 2(\bar b\cdot\bar c) = 4 + 16 + 16 - 0 = 36\), so the value is \(6\).

Area of kite PAOB \(= 2\times\frac12\times OA\times PA = 2\times\frac12\times 2\times 2\sqrt3 = 4\sqrt3\) sq. units.

131.solution:
Lines reduce to \(\frac{x-1}{3}=\frac{y+1}{3}=\frac{z-1}{5}\) and \(\frac{x+2}{4}=\frac{y-1}{3}=\frac{z+1}{2}\).
The determinant \(\begin{vmatrix} -3 & 2 & -2 \\ 3 & 3 & 5 \\ 4 & 3 & 2 \end{vmatrix} = 61 \neq 0\), so the lines do not intersect.

138.solution:
X = tosses until a number \(< n\) appears, a geometric distribution with success probability \(\frac{n-1}{n}\).
Mean \(= \frac{n}{n-1}\). Given mean \(= \frac{n}{9}\): \(\frac{n}{9} = \frac{n}{n-1} \Rightarrow n - 1 = 9 \Rightarrow n = 10\).

148.solution:
Let \(y = 81^{\sin^2 x}\). Then \(y + \frac{81}{y} = 30 \Rightarrow y^2 - 30y + 81 = 0 \Rightarrow y = 27\) or \(3\).
\(4\sin^2 x = 3\) or \(1 \Rightarrow \sin x = \frac{\sqrt3}{2}\) or \(\frac12\). In \([0,\pi]\), the listed values include \(\frac{\pi}{6},\frac{\pi}{3}\).

150.solution:
Curve crosses Y-axis at \((0,b)\); \(\frac{dy}{dx} = -\frac{b}{a}e^{-x/a}\), slope at \((0,b)\) is \(-\frac{b}{a}\).
Tangent: \(y - b = -\frac{b}{a}x \Rightarrow \frac{x}{a} + \frac{y}{b} = 1\).
